query: What are the common advantage attributes of airlines whose overall rating is high?

per_column.name: cabin_crew_attentiveness
per_column.rationale: Quality of in-flight crew interaction (friendly/attentive vs rude/dismissive) is an aspect OF an airline's service offering and thus a genuine part-of the competitive-advantage concept, not an external predictor of it.

per_column.name: seat_comfort_legroom
per_column.rationale: Physical seat/cabin comfort and pitch is a constitutive dimension of the airline product experience, a legitimate meronymic facet of competitive advantage.

per_column.name: customer_service_responsiveness
per_column.rationale: Responsiveness/helpfulness of service is an aspect OF the airline's offering, so it qualifies as a facet; however its underlying dimension (helpful vs dismissive service) substantially overlaps with cabin_crew_attentiveness.

judge.rationale: All three added columns are true constitutive facets (parts-of) the concept of airline competitive advantage: they each describe an aspect of the airline's product/service rather than an external cause or predictor. However, MECE is only moderately satisfied. Mutual exclusivity is weakened because cabin_crew_attentiveness and customer_service_responsiveness both capture essentially the same underlying dimension -- attentive/helpful vs dismissive/unresponsive service -- with near-identical value polarities (friendly_attentive/proactive_helpful vs rude_dismissive/dismissive_unhelpful), so the concept's 'service' aspect is double-counted. Exhaustiveness is limited: the columns effectively cover only two distinct aspects (interpersonal/service quality and seat comfort), while other clearly constitutive facets of an airline's competitive advantage -- food & beverages, inflight entertainment, value for money, punctuality/reliability, route network, and check-in/boarding/baggage handling -- are absent, leaving major parts of the concept uncovered.
